transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net customer technical support. My name is Hannah. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hello Hannah. I'm calling about our S-Net 4K TV box. When we tried to record our favorite documentary series last night, an error message popped up saying 'Error 7002: Hard disk write error - recording failed'.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can certainly help you troubleshoot that DVR hard disk error. May I have the account serial number listed on your customer bill?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, the account serial number is TV-884-219-01.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you. And what is the model number printed on the white label under the TV box?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It is model S-Net 4K Pro DVR 1TB. We have over forty hours of irreplaceable family holiday videos and historic sports matches stored on this disk, and my wife was practically in tears this morning thinking the entire hard drive has died!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I completely understand how devastating it would be to lose cherished family memories and sports recordings. Please do not worry, we have a specialized maintenance scan designed specifically to repair sector corruption without deleting your saved videos.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Oh, thank heaven for that! I was terrified we would have to factory format the whole drive.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: So if I have understood correctly, your S-Net 4K box is reporting Error 7002 disk write failure during scheduled recordings, and you require a non-destructive file system repair to recover storage operations while preserving your existing media library. Is that right?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, that is exactly what we need to accomplish today.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Error 7002 occurs when the Linux ext4 file allocation table encounters an unwritten journal block, typically after an unexpected mains power cut.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: We did have a brief electrical power flick on Sunday afternoon while the tumble dryer was running!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That explains the uncommitted journal transaction. We will boot the TV box into the S-Net Hardware Recovery Console to run an automated fsck integrity scan.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: How do we boot into that recovery console?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Please stand by the television box. On the front right panel, there is a small circular Standby button.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, I have my finger on the circular Standby button right now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Switch the rocker power switch on the back of the box to OFF, wait five seconds, then hold down the front Standby button while switching the power back ON.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Switching off... holding front button... switching on. Keep holding?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Keep holding the front button until the LED light pulses purple, then release it.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Pulsing purple now... releasing the button. The TV screen has switched to a black screen with an S-Net Recovery Diagnostics menu!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You will see four menu options: System Reboot, Non-Destructive Disk Repair, Factory Reset, and Firmware Flash.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, I see those four options on the television screen.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Use the directional arrow buttons on your remote to highlight Option 2: Non-Destructive Disk Repair, and press OK.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Highlighting Option 2: Non-Destructive Disk Repair... pressing OK. A progress bar appeared saying 'Checking file system journals and sector allocation'.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The utility is scanning the one-terabyte hard drive clusters, repairing orphan nodes, and remounting the write partition safely.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The progress bar is at 45%... 70%... now it says 'File system integrity restored - 0 lost clusters, 2 journal errors repaired'!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That is an ideal result! The file system journal has been cleanly resynchronized with zero data loss.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The TV box is rebooting automatically now. The home screen has loaded with our regular channel guide.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Press the My Recordings button on your remote control to verify your media library.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Pressing My Recordings... oh wonderful! All forty hours of our family holiday footage and documentary series are listed right there!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Try playing back one of the saved recordings to verify video playback throughput.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Selecting the holiday video... playing now. Sound and high-definition video are playing perfectly, no stuttering at all.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Obviously that confirms the disk head read mechanism and SATA controller are operating within factory tolerances.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Now let us test recording a live broadcast to confirm write operations.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Tune to channel 101 BBC One HD, press the red Record button on your remote control, and record five minutes of live TV.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Pressing Record on BBC One HD... a red recording circle appeared in the top corner of the screen without any error message!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let it record for sixty seconds, then stop the recording and play it back from the Recordings menu.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Stopping recording... going to Recordings... playing the new clip. It recorded the news segment cleanly with flawless picture and sound!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Just to check, is your home broadband connection and internet browsing working properly across your computers and mobile devices?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, our broadband has been fast and reliable, the issue was exclusively the TV box disk error.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let us also check the remaining disk capacity percentage under Settings to ensure storage health.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Navigating to Settings, then Storage Management... it shows 418 gigabytes free out of 1000 gigabytes, so 58% used.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That leaves ample recording headroom for dozens more hours of high-definition broadcasts.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Should we turn on automatic disk cleanup so older recordings don't accidentally fill up the remaining space?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I would advise keeping Auto-Delete set to 'Never' so your archived family holiday videos can never be overwritten automatically.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That is very sensible advice, I will definitely keep Auto-Delete turned off.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let us also check the standby power mode setting to help protect the hard drive from abrupt power transitions.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Under Standby Mode, we have options for Eco Mode and Active Standby. Which one is preferable?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Active Standby keeps the disk parked properly in a low-power quiescent state while still allowing scheduled midnight recordings to trigger smoothly.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I have selected Active Standby. The menu saved the preference.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let us also test the Series Link recording functionality from the TV guide to make sure future episodes queue up without error.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Going into TV Guide... selecting tonight's nature documentary... pressing Record Series. A green twin-ring icon appeared next to the programme title!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The twin-ring icon confirms the Series Link metadata has been registered in the local database.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Everything is functioning as smoothly as when the box was brand new.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I will remain the dedicated owner for this support case and log the non-destructive disk recovery on your equipment records.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you Hannah, you have saved our irreplaceable family videos today.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: If you ever experience a severe mains power cut in the future, remember that the Recovery Console Option 2 safely repairs the drive every time.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I have written down the button holding procedure on the front of our user manual.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Is there anything else with your S-Net TV box or broadband services that I can assist you with today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, that has resolved everything completely. Thank you again Hannah.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You may receive a brief customer satisfaction survey by SMS after this call; we would be very grateful if you could rate our service today.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I'll make sure to give you top ratings. Good afternoon.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for choosing S-Net. Have a wonderful rest of your day, and take care.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you, goodbye.
